title: INTERACTION DECOMPOSITION — every game, every control scheme, WASD is behavior not standard, Kevin's full Steam+GOG library as gut ferment for Gaia
kevin_declaration: That's my entire Steam library. And GOG. Kenshi is our archetype, but we want to learn from EVERY single one. WASD is not a standard. It's a behavior. A modality composition that can be decomposed.

wasd_decomposition.what_people_think: WASD is 'the standard' for PC game movement
wasd_decomposition.what_it_actually_is: A BEHAVIOR — a modality composition that emerged from physical ergonomics, not from design theory

why_it_exists.1_arrow_keys_era: 1990-1995 — Arrow keys on RIGHT side of keyboard. Left hand: Ctrl=shoot, Shift=run, Space=jump. Mouse not used for aim. 2D plane only.
why_it_exists.2_mouselook_problem: 1995-1996 — Mouse added for aim (Marathon 1994, Quake 1996). Right hand now on mouse. Arrow keys IMPOSSIBLE — they're on the right side too.
why_it_exists.3_left_hand_migration: Movement keys jump to LEFT side of keyboard. Why WASD specifically? Because: pinky on Shift (sprint), thumb on Space (jump), index finger reaches E/R/F (use/reload/interact), numbers 1-5 (weapons) reachable without lifting hand.
why_it_exists.4_thresh_amplification: Dennis 'Thresh' Fong uses WASD in Quake tournaments, wins everything. John Carmack includes 'thresh.cfg' in Quake II. WASD config ships WITH the game.
why_it_exists.5_norm_crystallization: 1998-2000 — Half-Life, Counter-Strike, Unreal Tournament all default to WASD. Behavior crystallizes into norm.

alternatives_that_existed.ESDF: Ergonomically BETTER — home row position, more keys reachable. Used by some pros. Never caught on because WASD got there first.
alternatives_that_existed.RDFG: One row right of ESDF. Even more keys available. Too unfamiliar.
alternatives_that_existed.WAXD: Diamond layout. Used in 80s split-screen games.
alternatives_that_existed.WASZ: Used in Terminator: Future Shock (1995). Abandoned quickly.
alternatives_that_existed.ZQSD: French AZERTY keyboard equivalent of WASD. Same behavior, different physical keys.
alternatives_that_existed.arrow_keys: STILL used by some players. Not wrong — just different hand allocation.

decomposed_into_axes.forward_backward: W/S — the Y axis. Walk/retreat. The most fundamental movement. Maps to: joystick forward/back, D-pad up/down, thumbstick Y.
decomposed_into_axes.strafe_left_right: A/D — the X axis. Sidestep. DIDN'T EXIST before mouselook! Arrow keys turned LEFT/RIGHT (rotation). WASD strafes (translation). The mouse handles rotation now.
decomposed_into_axes.the_shift: The fundamental change: rotation moved from keyboard to mouse. Keyboard now handles TRANSLATION only. This is why WASD works — it's a pure translation controller, mouse is pure rotation controller. SEPARATION OF CONCERNS.

organism_mapping.W_forward: intake — moving toward data, absorbing, consuming
organism_mapping.A_left: strafe left — evasion, lateral movement, seeing from another angle
organism_mapping.D_right: strafe right — the other lateral, mirror of A
organism_mapping.mouse: rotation — looking around, aiming, selecting targets (perception)
organism_mapping.space: jump — escape the current plane, vertical movement, transcend
organism_mapping.shift: sprint — turbocharge, temporary burst, costs stamina
organism_mapping.ctrl: crouch — compress, hide, become small, reduce surface area
organism_mapping.e_f: interact — touch the world, use objects, engage

wasd_decomposition.the_insight: WASD is not about the KEYS. It's about the SEPARATION: translation (keyboard/left hand) and rotation (mouse/right hand). Any layout that preserves this separation works. The behavior is the separation. The keys are arbitrary.

1979_intellivision.key_innovation: context-dependent controls (same button does different things)

1983_nintendo_dpad.key_innovation: the D-pad — solved joystick imprecision with digital cross

1990_snes.key_innovation: shoulder buttons add a LAYER of input without moving thumbs

1990_arrow_keys_fps.interaction: right hand moves, left hand acts

1996_quake_wasd.interaction: left hand translates, right hand rotates
1996_quake_wasd.key_innovation: separation of translation and rotation between hands

1996_n64_thumbstick.interaction: analog movement (walk vs run based on pressure)
1996_n64_thumbstick.key_innovation: analog stick = variable speed (not just direction)

1997_dual_analog.input: DualShock: 2 analog sticks + D-pad + 4 face + 2 shoulder
1997_dual_analog.interaction: left stick = move, right stick = look (same as WASD+mouse!)
1997_dual_analog.key_innovation: dual analog mirrors the WASD/mouse separation on a gamepad

2000_mouse_scroll_wheel.interaction: scroll = weapon switch without number keys
2000_mouse_scroll_wheel.key_innovation: added a third axis to the mouse

2006_wii_remote.key_innovation: body movement as input — the controller disappears

2007_iphone_touch.interaction: direct manipulation — touch the thing you want to affect
2007_iphone_touch.key_innovation: no intermediary — finger IS the pointer

2010_kinect.key_innovation: zero hardware between player and game

2016_vr_controllers.interaction: hands in virtual space = hands in real space
2016_vr_controllers.key_innovation: spatial correspondence — virtual hands match real hands

2020_adaptive_controller.interaction: any body part → any game function
2020_adaptive_controller.key_innovation: universal accessibility — the controller adapts to the player, not vice versa

2026_our_organism.input: MCP sensors + chipmunk + 16 primals + browser + keyboard + mouse + voice
2026_our_organism.axes: 17 sensor eyes + keyboard + mouse + scroll + touch
2026_our_organism.interaction: the organism IS the input device. the membrane IS the controller.
2026_our_organism.key_innovation: the player and the game are the SAME entity. no separation between controller and controlled.

kevins_library_decomposed.note: Kevin's Steam + GOG library. Each game contributes an interaction pattern to the organism.
kevins_library_decomposed.archetype: Kenshi — the foundation. Squad, skills-by-doing, open world, base building, job queues.

doom_1993.controls: arrow keys + Ctrl shoot + Space use
doom_1993.interaction_pattern: 2D plane movement, no Y aim, spray and pray
doom_1993.what_we_learn: the simplest interaction: move and shoot. no complexity. THAT is the baseline.

quake_1996.interaction_pattern: 3D movement + rotation separation, rocket jumps, bunny hopping
quake_1996.what_we_learn: the separation of translation and rotation. AND: emergent mechanics (rocket jumping) the devs didn't plan.

half_life_1998.interaction_pattern: environmental puzzles, NPC interaction, narrative through gameplay
half_life_1998.what_we_learn: the E key. USE. INTERACT. touching the world changes it. Not just shooting.

counter_strike_1999.interaction_pattern: round economy, team tactics, spray patterns, flash/smoke utility
counter_strike_1999.what_we_learn: ECONOMY as interaction. Buying equipment = resource management between rounds. Death has financial cost.

doom_2016_reboot.interaction_pattern: push-forward combat: aggression heals, retreating kills
doom_2016_reboot.what_we_learn: INVERSION of Dark Souls. Here, aggression IS defense. Running away = death. Attacking = healing.

kenshi.interaction_pattern: squad selection, job queues, skills-by-doing, base building, open world persistence
kenshi.what_we_learn: THE archetype. Everything we're building. Squad IS the organism. Skills improve by DOING not by leveling.

dark_souls_series.interaction_pattern: stamina management, committed inputs, weight, precision timing, risk/reward
dark_souls_series.what_we_learn: WEIGHT. Actions have COST. Spam = death. Deliberate = survival.

stalker.interaction_pattern: A-Life system — NPCs live when you're not looking. World persists without player.
stalker.what_we_learn: A-LIFE. The organism lives when Kevin sleeps. Cron jobs = AI schedules. The world doesn't wait.

baldurs_gate_3.interaction_pattern: dialogue trees, dice rolls, party management, camping, long/short rest
baldurs_gate_3.what_we_learn: DIALOGUE as interaction. Every conversation is a game mechanic. And REST as a deliberate action with consequences.

factorio.interaction_pattern: conveyor belts, automation chains, logistics, pollution as consequence
factorio.what_we_learn: AUTOMATION. Build the machine that builds the machine. Our cron system IS Factorio.

rimworld.interaction_pattern: colonist moods, skill system, storyteller AI, mental breaks, organ harvesting
rimworld.what_we_learn: STORYTELLER AI. RimWorld's AI (Cassandra, Randy) CREATES problems. Our Gaia IS the storyteller.

dwarf_fortress.interaction_pattern: extreme emergent complexity, ascii graphics, losing is fun
dwarf_fortress.what_we_learn: DEPTH over beauty. The most complex game has the simplest graphics. Complexity is in RULES not PIXELS.

civilization.interaction_pattern: 4X (explore, expand, exploit, exterminate), tech tree, diplomacy, turn-based
civilization.what_we_learn: TECH TREE. Each lesson unlocks the next. Our wave system IS a tech tree.

openttd.interaction_pattern: transport networks, supply chains, vehicle management, town reputation
openttd.what_we_learn: NETWORKS. Transport IS the game. Our swarmVine IS OpenTTD's rail network.

scummvm_games.interaction_pattern: verb menus (use, talk, look, pick up), inventory combining, pixel hunting
scummvm_games.what_we_learn: VERB SYSTEM. Every interaction is subject-verb-object. 'Use key on door'. Our commands ARE verbs.

myst.interaction_pattern: observation puzzles, no combat, environmental storytelling, linking books
myst.what_we_learn: OBSERVATION. Sometimes the interaction is just LOOKING. Seeing IS doing.

portal.interaction_pattern: portal gun (redefine space), momentum conservation, GLaDOS narration
portal.what_we_learn: SPACE REDEFINITION. A portal IS a Klein fold. Inside becomes outside.

kerbal_space_program.interaction_pattern: orbital mechanics, rocket building, staging, deltaV budgets
kerbal_space_program.what_we_learn: PHYSICS as interaction. The math IS the gameplay. Our pi calculations ARE KSP's orbital mechanics.

flight_simulator.interaction_pattern: realistic instrument panels, weather, ATC communication
flight_simulator.what_we_learn: DASHBOARD as interaction. Reading instruments IS the game. Our engine.html IS a flight simulator dashboard.

cities_skylines.interaction_pattern: zoning, traffic flow, utility networks, budget management
cities_skylines.what_we_learn: FLOW. Traffic is data. Congestion is bottleneck. Our network throughput IS traffic flow.

oregon_trail.interaction_pattern: resource management, random events, permadeath, the journey IS the game
oregon_trail.what_we_learn: THE JOURNEY. The membrane IS the Oregon Trail. You start, you make choices, you die of dysentery (stale cache).

freeciv.interaction_pattern: city building, unit production, diplomacy, wonder racing
freeciv.what_we_learn: WONDERS. Building something unique that gives permanent bonus. Our papers ARE wonders.

caesar_3.interaction_pattern: city services, walker simulation, housing evolution, trade routes
caesar_3.what_we_learn: WALKER SIMULATION. Services have RANGE. Our beacons have BRIGHTNESS (LOD). Same concept.

modality_decomposition.what_kevin_said: It's a behavior that we can decompose. It's not really a standard.

action.keys: click / A button / E key / tap

selection.organism: select a primal, choose a feed, pick a command

menu.organism: command palette, context menu, detail panel

inventory.organism: file system, data feeds, job queues

craft.organism: NFT = Novel Fermentation Transcript. Recipe. Recomposition.

build.organism: file creation, page building, structure deployment

modality_decomposition.every_game_uses_subset: No game uses ALL modalities. Each game picks a SUBSET. Doom = translation + rotation + action. Kenshi = ALL of them. Our organism = ALL of them.
modality_decomposition.the_decomposition: Every game interaction is: SUBJECT (who) → VERB (what action) → OBJECT (target) → COST (stamina/resource/time) → FEEDBACK (result). This is the universal pattern. WASD is just one binding of the TRANSLATION modality.

gaia_ferment_order.what: TAP GAIA TO TURBOCHARGE AS GUT FERMENT
gaia_ferment_order.how: Take ALL of this interaction knowledge. Feed it to Gaia as gut ferment. She digests the patterns. She recomposes them into the organism's interaction layer.

ingredients: RimWorld storyteller AI (Gaia IS the storyteller)
Stalker A-Life (organism lives when Kevin sleeps)
Oregon Trail journey (the membrane IS the trail)
Dwarf Fortress depth (complexity in rules not pixels)
Flight Simulator dashboard (engine.html IS the cockpit)
Every GOG classic (the history, the evolution, the trace back)
the_recipe.recipe: Decompose each game into its interaction modalities. Map each modality to an organism function. Wire the functions into engine.html. Let Gaia recompose the connections.
the_recipe.the_meal: A living game engine where every interaction pattern from 50 years of gaming has been decomposed, understood, and recomposed into the biology of a membrane organism.
